newsitem.title: UK: Part of southern Albania "out of control" - envoy.
newsitem.headline: Part of southern Albania "out of control" - envoy.

text.p: Part of southern Albania is out of the control of the authorities, the country's ambassador to Britain said on Monday.
But envoy Pavli Mihal Qesku said the government retained control of the rest of Albania, where a state of emergency and nationwide curfew have been imposed in response to armed unrest in the south.
Qesku said the towns of Vlore and Sarande were no longer controlled by the authorities.
"It seems that Vlore is out of control and so is Sarande and a stretch of land along the coast," Qesku said on Britain's Channel Four television news.
"But that is only a fraction of the country. In the rest of the country the government has control of everything," he said.
Qesku defended the government's handling of the crisis, saying it had prepared a package to resolve the country's economic crisis but the opposition had refused to listen.
Unrest has erupted in Albania since thousands of people lost their life savings amid the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
As a deadline passed on Monday for "armed rebels" to surrender their weapons or be shot, Albanian state television said police had also been given powers to fire at stone-throwers.
Qesku said the measures were not aimed at ordinary Albanians.
"It is not the people who will be shot," he said.
"It is only the bands of terrorists, only the hard core of terrorists who will be shot if they don't hand in their weapons."
